title: Pebble in Orbit
summary: Steer a student satellite with a magnet rod and a coil against Earth’s field: stop its spin, park it, turn it and dock a twin.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 5.2.3, The dipole in a uniform magnetic field
concepts: No net force in a uniform field
learningOutcome: The student can find the torque, potential energy and work for a magnet or coil in a uniform field, say why the net force is zero, and place two small magnets by their energy.

levels.title: Stop the spin
levels.adds: Baseline: τ = mB sin θ, largest at right angles to the field and zero along it; find m from a needed torque (Ex 5.1).
hints: τ = m B sin θ, where θ is the angle between m and B.
To find m, divide the torque by B sin θ.
Check the units: m is in J/T and B in µT, so τ comes out in µN m.

levels.title: Stable and unstable
levels.adds: New idea: U = −mB cos θ is lowest along the field (stable) and highest against it (unstable), with no torque at either (Ex 5.2).
hints: The torque is zero at θ = 0 and at θ = 180°.
U = −mB cos θ, which is −mB at 0° and +mB at 180°.
The moment points from the S end of the rod to its N end.

levels.title: Coast to the star
levels.adds: New idea: the work done to turn a magnet is the rise in its potential energy: mB to reach 90° and 2mB to reach 180° (Ex 5.5).
hints: From along the field, U goes from −mB to 0 at 90° and to +mB at 180°.
The torque mB sin θ is zero at 180°, though it took work to get there.

levels.title: The coil near the station
levels.adds: More steps: find m = NIA, then the torque; a uniform field gives no net force, a non-uniform one does (Ex 5.4, 5.6).
hints: m = N I A, with the area in m²: 1 cm² is 10⁻⁴ m².
In a uniform field the forces on the two ends are equal and opposite, so there is no net force.

levels.title: Twin dock
levels.adds: More steps: use the field of P (2k on its axis, k at right angles, opposite in direction there) to place Q (Example 5.2).
hints: On the axis of P, its field points the same way as m_P; at right angles to the axis it points the opposite way.
U = −m_Q·B_P: lowest when m_Q points along the strongest field.
If m_Q is across the field of P there is a torque on it: not equilibrium.

misconceptions: A magnet in a uniform field feels a net force
The torque on a magnet is largest when it is aligned with the field
The potential energy of a magnet along the field is zero
Opposite poles side by side are an unstable arrangement
